If that happened to you, we can connect you with an independent attorney who handles premises liability claims at no upfront cost.

about.title: Vernon Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Vernon is built around industry — warehouses, meatpacking facilities, distribution centers, and the businesses that serve workers moving through them near S Santa Fe Avenue, District Boulevard, and S Soto Street. That mix of freight traffic, loading areas, and older commercial buildings creates plenty of spots where spills, uneven pavement, or poor lighting can go unaddressed. Under California law, a property owner or occupier can be held responsible for a fall if they knew, or reasonably should have known, about a hazardous condition and didn't fix it or warn visitors. Proving that notice element is often the hardest part of a premises liability case, which is why documenting the scene and getting surveillance footage preserved quickly matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects injured people with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened and advise on next steps, working on contingency so there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Vernon Fall Victims Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California premises cases hinge on showing the property owner knew, or should have known, about the hazard. An attorney in our network can help identify evidence — like prior complaint records or maintenance logs — that speaks to that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Warehouses and commercial lots in Vernon commonly run security cameras that overwrite footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having video evidence and losing it.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for how the fall happened, you may still be able to recover a reduced amount. An independent attorney can walk you through how that could apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Vernon?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government or public entity, that window is much shorter and requires an early claim filing, so it's worth having an attorney check the specifics soon after the incident.

items.question: What should I do right after falling on someone else's property in Vernon?
items.answer: If you're able, photograph the hazard, the surrounding area, and any wet floor or warning signs (or lack of them) before conditions change. Ask that the location's security video be preserved, since many Vernon warehouses and businesses run on short retention cycles. Getting medical attention promptly also creates a record tying your injury to the incident.

items.question: Does it matter that Vernon is mostly industrial and commercial property?
items.answer: It can. Many falls here happen at loading docks, warehouse floors, or business parking areas rather than private homes, which often means dealing with a commercial property manager, employer, or insurer rather than an individual homeowner. An independent attorney can help sort out which party or policy applies to your specific fall.
